newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian industry said to post negative growth.
newsitem.headline: Colombian industry said to post negative growth.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 15 Reuter - Colombian industrial output fell minus one percent in February compared to the same month last year, according to a closely watched private sector survey.
The survey, by the National Association of Industrialists ANDI, said the negative growth figure followed a 4.0 percent increase in industrial production in January.
February's drop back into negative territory was partly due to "permanent changes" in government economic policy that added a climate of widespread uncertainty, ANDI said.

It did not elaborate, but a package of emergency economic measures unveiled by the government in January was struck down by a high court in mid-February on grounds that the government had violated the constitution in imposing the measures by decree.

The ANDI survey, based on interviews with industrialists across the country, also cited flagging demand, loan portfolio problems, high financial costs and Colombia's booming trade in contraband goods as among leading reasons for the drop in industrial output.
